newsitem.title: USA: Glickman not in favor of CRP contract extention.
newsitem.headline: Glickman not in favor of CRP contract extention.

text.p: WASHINGTON, Sept 27 (Rueter) - Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said Friday that he would not favor special extensions of Conservation Reserve Program contracts, as House Agriculture Commmitee chairman Pat Roberts (R-Kan.) has called for.

Glickman said there will likely be some slight changes to the announced program, but said he would not endorse Roberts' move to include in an omnibus spending bill provisions that would extend CRP contracts.
"Quite frankly I think we're better going through the procedures of the 45-day rule making ... I would prefer that we not lurch back to the other process," Glickman told reporters.
Senate Agriculture Committee chairman Richard Lugar said Thursday he strongly opposed any efforts to change the CRP.
Glickman said that Roberts' claims that 24 million acres of fragile farmland would come out of the CRP if allowed to expire are wrong, and that USDA estimates are significantly lower.

Glickman also stressed that any buyouts of staff people in the Farm Service Agency, which implements the CRP, will not impact funds available to the CRP, nor affect enrollement in the program. Sen. Larry Pressler (R-SD) has charged that USDA plans to use CRP funds to pay for employee buyouts, which would deplete the budget to carry out the program.
